ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Satchel Paige

code.originalText: Two-week review on the day of the pulmonology consultation: spirometry with race-neutral interpretation, blood gas, six-minute walk, GOLD group and first maintenance inhaler, inhaler technique, pulmonary rehabilitation and lung cancer screening

text.paragraph: Two-week review on the day of the pulmonology consultation. [S]

Mr. Paige returns two weeks after intake and was seen this morning by Dr. Lindqvist-Bello of pulmonology, who did spirometry before and after albuterol, an arterial blood gas and a six-minute walk. He uses his albuterol once or twice a day, mostly before walking to the store, with the spacer. He is still breathless after one flight of stairs or a block on the level and coughs up a little clear sputum each morning. He has had no flare-ups in the past year. He takes atorvastatin each evening without muscle aches. He asked to see his breathing numbers and how they were worked out, and said he had read that lung tests used to be scored differently for Black patients; Dr. Lindqvist-Bello went through the results with him. [S]

list.item:
COPD, GOLD grade 2, group B (J44.9). Dr. Lindqvist-Bello confirms COPD: a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.58, below 0.70 and below the lower limit of normal. With the race-neutral GLI Global equations his FEV1 is 61% of predicted, GOLD grade 2; race-specific equations for Black men would have predicted a lower normal value and put him at about 70%, understating his impairment. A CAT of 18 and mMRC of 2 with no exacerbation in the past year place him in GOLD group B, for which a LAMA with a LABA is the first maintenance treatment. With eosinophils of 0.08 x 10^3/uL and no exacerbations, an inhaled corticosteroid would add risk without benefit. His PaO2 of 70 mm Hg and lowest walking saturation of 90 percent mean he needs no long-term or ambulatory oxygen. [S]
Umeclidinium 62.5 micrograms with vilanterol 25 micrograms, one inhalation each morning.
Albuterol as needed.
Pulmonary rehabilitation twice a week for about ten weeks.
Low-dose CT for lung cancer screening after shared decision-making.
A COPD action plan, spoken and written.

Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin (E78.5). Two weeks on atorvastatin without muscle symptoms. [S]
Lipid panel at the eight-week visit.

Follow-up: Start the new inhaler tomorrow morning. Low-dose CT in one week. Rehabilitation from the second week of August. Eight-week review with a lipid panel. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-08: eight-week review: symptoms on the new inhaler, technique, rehabilitation, the screening CT and the lipid response. [S]
